def.label: Mk1 thermal sight
def.note: Doc 16 section 9 item 3's sight, and every number is the same axis: it reads a plume, not a shape. max_range_cells 45 against the Mk1 visual's 60 -- a thermal channel is shorter-legged than a daylight optic. max_attenuation 30 passes one belt of light woods (the atlas prices it 25) and stops at a canopy (60), which is tighter than the eye's 40 because foliage is opaque in this band. classify_after_ms 5,000 against 3,000: a hot blob takes longer to tell apart than an outline. sees_wrecks false for a new reason -- a burnt-out hull goes cold. THE SIGNATURE TABLE is deliberately flatter than the visual sight's: the ground hides a silhouette and does very little to a heat source, so heavy woods stopped is 880 here against 500 there. What replaces it is the thermal term the mount carries (16b cut X.3): an idling tank is dim and a shut-down one is nearly dark, whatever it is standing in.
